procedural_markers.speaker: Court Clerk
procedural_markers.text: Your  Honor, for the purpose of the record, we return back to the trial of  Commonwealth versus Lindsay Clancy. All parties are present, including  the defendant and including all 18 jurors.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: All  Right. Thank you, Madam Clerk. Members of the jury, we're now going to  return, as I told you before, to the Commonwealth's case and I'll ask  the Commonwealth to call their next witness.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: The Commonwealth would call Mark Anthony Maffeo to the stand.

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: While we're waiting, Your Honor, just for the record, same objection and standing objection so that keeps ...

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: Can you stop right here, raise your right hand?

procedural_markers.speaker: Court Clerk
procedural_markers.text: Good  morning. Do you solemnly swear that the testimony and the evidence you  shall [inaudible 00:01:52] between the Commonwealth and the [inaudible  00:01:52] shall be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the  truth, so help you God?

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: I have no objection to the photographs, Your Honor.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: May I approach the witness?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: All right. Those may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: Sir,  if I could just draw your attention to the screen beside you. I'm  showing you now what's been marked as Exhibit 110. And who was the  individual depicted in this photograph?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: And showing you on the screen what's been marked as Exhibit number 111. Again, is that Lindsay Clancy?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: And  112, Exhibit 112. In the middle of this photograph with an arm  extended, there are some cuts and a cut in the middle. Did you observe  those on January 24th as well?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: And finally, Exhibit 113. That would be the other arm. Did you observe those cuts to that arm?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: May I approach again?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: Any objection?

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: I have no objection to any of the photographs.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: They may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: Sustained.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: Any objection?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: May we approach?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: Sure. Yeah. All right, that may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: All right, that may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge
procedural_markers.text: All right. All right. Those photos may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: Thank  you. And I'm just showing you another exhibit. This would have already  been introduced into evidence, and this would be Exhibit 112. And this  would also depict the area of the wrist. Is that correct?

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: The cut was ... likewise, Exhibit 111 also shows the cuts on the neck. Is that correct?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: Any objection?

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: I just admitted them through Sergeant Murphy.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: No objection.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: All right. That may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Richard Lippard
procedural_markers.text: Exhibit 126.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: All right. Any objection to that?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: All right. Those pictures may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: Attorney Buckingham, any redirect?

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: Could you stop right here and raise your right hand for the clerk, please.

procedural_markers.speaker: Clerk
procedural_markers.text: Good  afternoon. Do you solemnly swear that the testimony you're about to  give [inaudible 00:28:57] the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but  the truth, so help you God?

procedural_markers.speaker: Counsel
procedural_markers.text: Objection.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 2
procedural_markers.text: Overruled.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 2
procedural_markers.text: All right. Thank you, sir. You may step down. Thank you.

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: Commonwealth calls Dr. Tenerowicz.

procedural_markers.speaker: Counsel
procedural_markers.text: Do you want to go to sidebar?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 2
procedural_markers.text: All right. [inaudible 00:39:14] break. I'm sorry.

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: Good afternoon. Do you solemnly swear [inaudible 00:39:41]?

procedural_markers.speaker: Counsel
procedural_markers.text: And after ... Well, strike that. Did you observe any trauma to his body?

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: Commonwealth  will call Dr. Benjamin Kaufman. Good afternoon. Do you solemnly swear  that the testimony and the evidence you shall give to the court shall be  the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, so help you God?

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: Just for the record, Your Honor, I'd like to just note same objection.

procedural_markers.speaker: Dr. Benjamin Kaufman
procedural_markers.text: So  at no point did he exhibit any brain function. I'm not a neurologist,  so we are not the definitive person, but in emergency medicine, there's a  scale called the Glasgow Coma Scale, which is generally from three to  15. There's different variations for pediatrics, but he scored the  lowest, which basically is you're in a coma or have no brain response  during the entire time that he was in my care.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: Your Honor, the Commonwealth would call Melissa Arcadipane.

procedural_markers.speaker: Bailiff
procedural_markers.text: [inaudible 00:51:23]. Stop right there and raise your right hand for the clerk, please.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 5
procedural_markers.text: Good  afternoon. Do you solemnly swear the testimony and the evidence you  shall give to the court and the jury [inaudible 00:52:06]?

procedural_markers.speaker: Kevin Reddington
procedural_markers.text: No objection.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge William Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: All right, they may be admitted.

procedural_markers.speaker: Ms. Buckingham
procedural_markers.text: If we could approach sidebar?

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge William Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: Jury,  in talking to counsel, we are going to break for today, all right? What  I was talking about over here is in regards to the schedule where we  are. We are, if not on schedule, at a schedule, all right? And much of  it is because of the work when you're not here. Counsel's going over  some of the exhibits and some of that, and that's part of some of these  breaks, at least for you, all right? So I just want to let you know  that's what's going on. So I'm going to excuse you. I know it's been a  long week anyway. So we're going to take a break till Monday, all right?  And on Monday, the schedule anticipation will start about 9: 00, maybe a  little bit later than that, but I ask you to be here ready to go at  9:00. There's some matters I may have to talk to counsel, so it might  give a you little bit late start for you on Monday. And then the  anticipations will go most of the day, all right? ([58:47](https://www.rev.com/app/transcript/NmE2ZTBkYmU3OWFjZmJmNWUyMWUyYmE3Vk1TcnYtVUFSMlY4/o/VEMwMzI1ODM0MTM3?ts=3527.58)) Like  I said, we are well on schedule, if not ahead. What I want to remind  you now, which you know I'm going to remind you, that you're going to be  not here for a couple of days, it's very important. You've heard some  of the evidence, you haven't heard all of the evidence, all right? You  haven't heard the law that you will apply to this. So you have to keep  an open mind. And the best way to do that is don't talk about this with  anyone. Don't do any research. Don't watch anything. If something comes  on, turn it off. And just like I said, if you're talking to somebody who  brings it up, blame me, all right? "The judge said I am not to talk  about it, I'm not to listen to anybody talking about this," and shut  them down right away. I appreciate all the work that you've put in here  so far. I look forward to seeing you on Monday. I hope you have a nice  weekend and we'll see you then. All right, thank you.

procedural_markers.speaker: Judge William Sullivan
procedural_markers.text: All right. So we'll be in recess on this matter until Monday morning. At 9:00, we'll resume the trial. Thank you.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 4
